📌 Zero-Knowledge Proofs (ZK): Proving Facts Without Revealing Data

Main Points
⏺ Zero-knowledge proofs let you prove something is true without showing the underlying data
⏺ They power private transactions, identity checks, and scalable rollups
⏺ This post explains why ZK is one of the most important cryptography tools in Web3

1️⃣ Core Idea — you convince a verifier that a statement is true (for example, “I’m over 18”) without revealing the raw info (like your birthday)
2️⃣ Privacy — ZK helps hide amounts, identities, or logic while still keeping systems verifiable
3️⃣ Scalability — zk-rollups bundle many transactions and prove their correctness with a single compact proof
4️⃣ UX Examples — private voting, anonymous KYC, or proofs of funds without doxxing your full wallet
5️⃣ Trade-Offs — ZK systems can be complex to implement and sometimes expensive to compute, but they keep improving

Final Thoughts

Zero-knowledge proofs let Web3 be both verifiable and private — showing that something is valid without dumping all your data on-chain.

Berlin’s Two Rebellions

Berlin’s election lifted two parties that reject the political center, though they offer opposite answers to the same problems: soaring rents, falling confidence and a city where the established parties seem fluent in explanation but short on relief.

Die Linke finished first with 25.3%, ahead of the CDU on 19% and the AfD on 16%. Its lead candidate, Elif Eralp, campaigned on bringing roughly 220,000 apartments owned by large corporate landlords into public ownership. 

In Berlin’s 2021 referendum, 58% voted to expropriate major real-estate companies. The cost could range from €7 billion to €36 billion. Berlin’s Social Democrats estimate roughly €20 billion.

Bild calls the plan a lie. Eralp says it would take speculation out of Berlin’s housing market. Rent has more than doubled in the city over the past 13 years. That turned housing into the issue that mattered most at the ballot box.

The AfD’s 16% came from another kind of revolt. It promises to end weapons deliveries to Kyiv, lift sanctions on Moscow and restore access to cheap Russian energy. 

Die Linke offers public ownership. The AfD offers lower energy costs. Merz offers a security agenda and warnings about Russia. Berlin voters rewarded the parties that named an immediate household cost.

Die Linke still needs coalition partners, and the housing plan faces legal, financial and political barriers. But the election delivered a verdict on the governing center. 

Germans have been asked to bear higher prices in the name of security, Ukraine and fiscal discipline. Berlin’s vote showed what happens when rent becomes more urgent than geopolitics.

⚡️ Derivatives liquidations contributed to the initial acceleration. More than $34.5 million in ZEC short positions were reportedly closed during a 24-hour period as bearish traders were forced to buy back the asset. Short liquidations accounted for about 94% of the total cited liquidations. Forced buying helped ZEC clear resistance quickly, but the same leverage that drove the advance could increase volatility if traders begin taking profits.
